previous_statement: Because R=U union V is nonempty, e_R is a nonzero coordinate projection of C^m and ||e_R||=1. The two-sided norm bounds in the definition of the extended t-inclusion w give (1-t)||e_R|| <= ||w(e_R)|| <= (1+t)||e_R||. Hence 1-t <= ||P_R|| <= 1+t and therefore | ||P_R||-1 | <= t <= t+epsilon_A. Since P_R is already a t-projection, this is the nonvanishing (second norm) alternative with the explicit universal coefficient 1; it does not follow merely from P_R != 0 and uses no hidden O(t) constant.
